# Hazard thresholds, as the pipeline classifies them

**Generated by `scripts/generate_threshold_table.R` on 2026-10-07 — do not hand-edit.**
Source: `metadata/haz_classes.csv` (thresholds), `metadata/haz_metadata.csv` (units and hazard type).

A hazard fires for a cell-year when the index crosses the threshold in the stated direction.
The three severity classes are nested in intent but are classified independently.

> **The live V1 'Evaluate Climate Risks' notebook shows the `severe` class only.** It is hard-wired
> to that class; the moderate and extreme columns below are published but not surfaced there (#20).

## Generic crop hazards

These are the thresholds behind the published `NDWS+NTx35+NDWL0` set, which is what the live V1
notebook reads.

| hazard | index | moderate | severe | extreme |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cold | `TAVG` | < 18 °C | < 10 °C | < 6 °C |
| dry | `NDD` | > 15 day | > 20 day | > 25 day |
| dry | `NDWS` | > 15 day | > 20 day | > 25 day |
| dry | `PTOT` | < 500 mm | < 400 mm | < 300 mm |
| dry | `TAI` | > 40 | > 60 | > 80 |
| heat | `HSH_max` | > 27 °C | > 32 °C | > 41 °C |
| heat | `HSH_mean` | > 27 °C | > 32 °C | > 41 °C |
| heat | `NTx35` | > 7 day | > 14 day | > 21 day |
| heat | `NTx40` | > 1 day | > 5 day | > 10 day |
| heat | `TAVG` | > 33 °C | > 36 °C | > 47 °C |
| wet | `NDWL0` | > 2 day | > 5 day | > 8 day |
| wet | `PTOT` | > 1200 mm | > 1600 mm | > 1800 mm |

## Crop-specific heat thresholds

Three heat index families are derived **per crop** from `metadata/ecocrop.csv` at run time
(`R/2_calculate_haz_freq.R` §0.2.2.1), so they do not appear in `haz_classes.csv`:

| family | temperature threshold | exceedance days (mod / sev / ext) |
|---|---|---|
| `NTxM` | `Temp_Opt_Max` | 7 / 14 / 21 |
| `NTxS` | `ceil((Temp_Opt_Max + Temp_Abs_Max) / 2)` | 7 / 14 / 21 |
| `NTxE` | `Temp_Abs_Max` | 1 / 5 / 10 |

Worked example, maize (`Zea mays`: `Temp_Opt_Max` = 33, `Temp_Abs_Max` = 47): `NTxM` = 33 °C, `NTxS` = 40 °C, `NTxE` = 47 °C.

**`NTxM` is the family wired into the published crop-specific sets** (changed from `NTxS` in
2026-10, issue #25: `NTxS` averages the optimum with the *survival* limit, which for maize gives
40 °C and reported zero heat-exposed value). All three are classified; only the wired one reaches
a published hazard set. Ecocrop is an ecological envelope rather than an agronomic one, so these
are under review (#14, #24, #25).

## Published hazard sets

Each set is a three-way interaction of a dry, a heat and a wet index. The `hazard_vars` column of
the published parquet carries these strings.

| `hazard_vars` | heat | dry / wet framing | applies to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NDWS+NTx35+NDWL0` | generic, 35 °C | water balance | crops — **this is what the live V1 notebook reads** |
| `NDWS+NTxM+NDWL0` | crop-specific | water balance | crops (new in 2026-10, #25) |
| `PTOT-L+NTxM+PTOT-G` | crop-specific | precipitation total | crops (was `PTOT-L+NTxS+PTOT-G`) |
| `NDWS+THI-max+NDWL0` | species-specific | water balance | livestock |
| `PTOT-L+THI-max+PTOT-G` | species-specific | precipitation total | livestock |

Definitions of each index: the hazards wiki. THI provenance: `metadata/THI_thresholds_provenance.md`.
